stops.name: cpu
stops.mechanism: RLIMIT_CPU (setrlimit) + SIGXCPU, SIGKILL at the hard limit

stops.name: wall
stops.mechanism: an in-child watchdog thread that calls os._exit, inside the launcher's own -t limit
stops.outer_stop: the launcher's -t wall limit, which does not depend on the child

stops.name: host_envelope
stops.mechanism: the cgroup's MemoryMax, set by the launcher; the kernel kills the tree

stops.name: device_envelope
stops.mechanism: tf.config.set_logical_device_configuration, predeclared before device init: an oversized request fails with ResourceExhaustedError where it is made
stops.not_this: an allocator statistic compared later, which is OBSERVED_AFTER_THE_FACT

stops.name: stage:probe
stops.mechanism: setitimer(ITIMER_REAL) for the stage wall and a CPU poll that exits

stops_declared.reading: each row names the mechanism that stops the run. A budget with no mechanism is not a stop and does not appear here

cpu_stop.name: cpu
cpu_stop.mechanism: RLIMIT_CPU (setrlimit) + SIGXCPU, SIGKILL at the hard limit
cpu_stop.hard_stop: SIGKILL at the hard limit, which the child cannot decline

wall_stop.name: wall
wall_stop.mechanism: an in-child watchdog thread that calls os._exit at the deadline
wall_stop.outer_stop: the launcher's own -t wall limit and the supervisor's timeout

device_envelope.scope: FRAMEWORK_ALLOCATOR/DEVICE: the TensorFlow allocator's own accounting for one GPU device, from tf.config.experimental.get_memory_info. It is DEVICE memory held by TensorFlow and it is never added to any other scope
device_envelope.bounds: the TensorFlow allocator's arena on this device
device_envelope.does_not_bound: the CUDA context, cuDNN/cuBLAS workspaces outside the arena, and any other tenant of the device: those are WHOLE_DEVICE scope
device_envelope.why: the framework registered 0 device(s), so index 0 cannot be capped

device_verification.reading: a GPU placement was declared and no device is visible to this process. `run_units` passes CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" to every child, so a pilot sealed against that runner is a CPU pilot and may not be reported as a GPU one

reset_before.reset_basis: the following peak on this device is the peak SINCE THIS RESET

framework_allocator.scope: FRAMEWORK_ALLOCATOR/HOST: the TensorFlow allocator's own accounting for CPU:0, from tf.config.experimental.get_memory_info where that build exposes it. It is HOST RAM held by TensorFlow's own allocator -- not device memory, not the cgroup's watermark, and it is never added to any other scope
framework_allocator.scope_rule: its own scope, its own basis, its own name; two scopes are never added and merge_scopes refuses to
framework_allocator.peak_basis: the maximum this device's TensorFlow allocator has held since the process started or since the last reset_memory_stats on this device

envelope_observation.scope: FRAMEWORK_ALLOCATOR/HOST: the TensorFlow allocator's own accounting for CPU:0, from tf.config.experimental.get_memory_info where that build exposes it. It is HOST RAM held by TensorFlow's own allocator -- not device memory, not the cgroup's watermark, and it is never added to any other scope
envelope_observation.reading: a comparison made AFTER the allocator already held the memory. It reports an exceedance; it never prevents one. The enforceable limit is the predeclared allocator configuration, and the two are different claims
envelope_observation.why: a GPU:0 envelope may not be compared with a figure measured on CPU:0: one is device memory and the other is host RAM held by the framework. Two scopes, and a comparison across them passes nothing

framework_allocator.scope: FRAMEWORK_ALLOCATOR/HOST: the TensorFlow allocator's own accounting for CPU:0, from tf.config.experimental.get_memory_info where that build exposes it. It is HOST RAM held by TensorFlow's own allocator -- not device memory, not the cgroup's watermark, and it is never added to any other scope
framework_allocator.scope_rule: its own scope, its own basis, its own name; two scopes are never added and merge_scopes refuses to
framework_allocator.peak_basis: the maximum this device's TensorFlow allocator has held since the process started or since the last reset_memory_stats on this device

host_cgroup.scope: HOST_CGROUP: memory.peak of this cell's own cgroup -- the whole process tree's host RAM high-watermark as the kernel charges it, and it is never added to any other scope
host_cgroup.scope_rule: its own scope, its own basis, its own name; two scopes are never added and merge_scopes refuses to
host_cgroup.basis: memory.peak of this cell's own cgroup
host_cgroup.why: this scope was not read for this record: ABSENT, not zero

process_rss.scope: PROCESS_RESIDENT_SET: getrusage(RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss of this process alone. Host RAM, one process, no children, no kernel accounting, and it is never added to any other scope
process_rss.scope_rule: its own scope, its own basis, its own name; two scopes are never added and merge_scopes refuses to

whole_device.scope: WHOLE_DEVICE: memory in use on the physical device by every process, as the driver reports it. It includes contexts and other tenants and it is never added to any other scope
whole_device.scope_rule: its own scope, its own basis, its own name; two scopes are never added and merge_scopes refuses to
whole_device.why: this scope was not read for this record: ABSENT, not zero

record.merge_rule: four scopes, four bases, four names. No field in this record is the sum of two of them, and merge_scopes refuses to produce one
record.missing_rule: a figure that could not be read is UNKNOWN. Never 0 and never a success
